issue.standard_remedy: Consolidate tail suppliers into preferred suppliers
issue.summary: 97 of 117 suppliers share the last 20% of category spend

plan.diagnosis: The Maintenance spares category exhibits severe tail fragmentation: 97 of 117 suppliers (83%) account for only $3,023,013 (20%) of the $15,378,040 total spend, while the top supplier (Schwaben United Supply Corp.) holds just 17.4% share. The low HHI of 840 and inefficient supplier base create unnecessary transaction costs, duplicate overhead, and limit leverage for volume discounts.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct spend analysis across all ERPs (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Coupa) to map the 97 tail suppliers by part number overlap and identify consolidation candidates under Schwaben United Supply Corp. and 2-3 other preferred suppliers
Issue RFQ to top 5 suppliers by spend requesting volume-tiered pricing for consolidated tail spend of $3,023,013, targeting 12-15% savings through economies of scale
Negotiate master agreements with 2-3 selected preferred suppliers covering 90% of tail SKUs, establishing payment terms of Net 60 and committed annual volume tiers
Communicate supplier rationalization plan to requisitioners and implement source list restrictions in all ERPs, blocking non-preferred tail suppliers for covered SKUs
Execute cutover: redirect POs from 85+ tail suppliers to preferred suppliers, monitor service levels and part availability for 90 days

plan.expected_impact: Consolidating tail spend is expected to generate $362,000 to $453,000 in annual savings (12-15% of $3,023,013) plus reduce processing costs by eliminating 85+ low-value supplier relationships.
kpis: Supplier count reduction (target: 117 to 30 or fewer)
Average PO value in category (measure transaction efficiency gain)
risks: Part availability gaps if preferred suppliers cannot cover full tail SKU catalog
Requisitioner resistance and maverick buying if source restrictions enforced too quickly
Service level degradation during transition causing production downtime
Incumbent tail suppliers may hold proprietary or OEM-specific parts requiring exemptions
Cross-ERP data quality issues may obscure true part number equivalencies and delay consolidation
erp_actions: SAP: Apply posting block in LFB1 for 85+ tail suppliers in relevant company codes after cutover; update source lists (ME01) to restrict materials to preferred suppliers only
Oracle EBS: Set supplier sites to 'Hold All Payments' status and mark as inactive in approved supplier list (ASL) for consolidated categories
Dynamics 365: Update procurement categories to limit vendor associations; configure purchasing policies to enforce preferred supplier sourcing rules
NetSuite: Inactivate tail vendor records and create item-vendor relationships restricting maintenance spares to 2-3 preferred suppliers

Coupa: Update supplier status to 'Do Not Use' for tail suppliers; configure catalog and sourcing events to feature preferred suppliers with contracted pricing; set payment terms to Net 60 for preferred suppliers
